privacy.title: Privacy Policy
intro: This is the Privacy Policy for https://minecraftsgame.com/. It sets out what personal data we collect, why we collect it, and what rights you have over it. Have a read before you sign up — if something here doesn't sit right with you, the safest option is not to use the Website or Services.
Using the Website or Services means you accept what's described below.

sections.heading: Who Controls Your Data
paragraphs: Dexervil LTD is the data controller for the purposes of the GDPR — in plain terms, we decide what data is collected and why, and we're the ones responsible if something goes wrong.

sections.heading: What We Collect
paragraphs: What we hold on you depends on how you use the Services. It generally falls into these buckets:
bullets: Account Information — your login details, username, activity logs, settings, and anything else in your profile.
Contact Details — email address, and phone number or postal address if you've given us one.
Transaction Information — your order history and account balance.
Payment Data — handled entirely by our payment processor, FINTECH GLOBAL SOFTWARE LTD. We never see your full card details; the processor collects and handles that directly, under PCI-DSS.
Communication Records — whatever you've told our support team, and their replies.
Technical Information — device type, IP address, OS, browser, and similar.
Customer Support Data — the issues you've reported and how they were sorted out.
Marketing Preferences — whether, and how, you'd like to hear from us.

sections.heading: Why We Use It
paragraphs: Each purpose below comes with a legal basis attached, since GDPR requires one:
bullets: Service Provision — delivering what you asked for (contract).
Account Management — setting up and running your account (contract).
Order Fulfilment — processing and delivering purchases (contract).
Transaction Management — handling payments securely (contract, legitimate interests).
Customer Support — answering questions and fixing problems (contract, legitimate interests).
Legal Compliance — meeting obligations we're legally bound by (legal obligation).
Fraud Prevention — spotting and stopping misuse (legal obligation, legitimate interests).
Service Improvement — making the Website and Services better over time (legitimate interests).
Marketing — only where you've said yes (consent).

sections.heading: What's Required and What's Optional
paragraphs: Some fields are compulsory — we'll flag those when you're asked for them, and without them we may not be able to provide certain Services. Everything else is optional and just helps us tailor things to you.

sections.heading: How We Get Your Data
paragraphs: Directly from you — when you register, buy something, or contact us.
Automatically — through cookies and similar tools as you browse. See our Cookie Policy for the details.
From third parties — occasionally, from partners such as our payment provider.

sections.heading: Who We Share It With
paragraphs: We share personal data with:
bullets: service providers who help us with payments, analytics, or support, all bound by their own data protection obligations;
regulators or public authorities, where the law requires it;
anyone else, but only if you've asked us to or given us clear consent.

sections.heading: We Don't Sell Your Data
paragraphs: We don't sell your data. Full stop.

sections.heading: Keeping Your Data Safe
paragraphs: We use encryption (both in transit and at rest), access controls, and regular reviews to keep things secure. No system is bulletproof, though — so use a strong, unique password, and turn on two-factor authentication if it's on offer.

sections.heading: Sending Data Outside the EEA
paragraphs: If we ever need to move your data outside the European Economic Area, we put safeguards in place first — typically the European Commission's Standard Contractual Clauses — so the protection travels with the data.

sections.heading: Your Rights
paragraphs: Under data protection law, you can:
bullets: Access — ask for a copy of what we hold on you.
Correct — have inaccurate or incomplete data fixed.
Delete — ask us to erase your data, subject to any legal reason we might have to keep it.
Restrict — ask us to limit how we use it in certain situations.
Object — push back on processing based on our legitimate interests, or on direct marketing.
Port — get your data in a format you can take elsewhere.
Withdraw consent — at any time, where consent was the basis, without affecting anything already done.

sections.heading: Making a Request
paragraphs: To use any of these, just email us — we may need to check who you are first.

sections.heading: Automated Decisions
paragraphs: We don't make decisions that carry legal or similarly serious consequences for you purely by algorithm, with no human involved.

sections.heading: If You're Under 18
paragraphs: Our Services aren't meant for anyone under 18. We don't knowingly collect data from minors, and if we find out we have, we'll delete it. If you think a minor has given us their data, let us know.

sections.heading: How Long We Keep It
paragraphs: We hold onto personal data only as long as we actually need it for the purposes above, or as the law requires — generally matching the limitation period for potential legal claims. After that, it's deleted or anonymised.

sections.heading: Complaints
paragraphs: If something's bothering you about how we're handling your data, talk to us first. You're also free to complain to the data protection authority where you live.

sections.heading: Changes to This Policy
paragraphs: We may update this Policy now and then, to reflect changes in what we do or in the law. If a change is significant, we'll let you know via the Website or by email. Carrying on using the Services after that means you're fine with the update.

sections.heading: Get in Touch
paragraphs: Questions about this Policy? Email us at privacy@minecraftsgame.com.

sections.heading: Our Services

Through your Personal Cabinet, you can buy privileges, crystals, and other Digital Items — pick a Server at checkout, and that's where your purchase lands.

sections.heading: Server Access
paragraphs: Getting onto our Servers is free, but you'll need a genuine, licensed copy of the Game. Fire up the Game, drop the relevant Server's IP address into the multiplayer menu — you'll find the addresses on the Website. Switching Servers just means grabbing the new IP from the Website.

sections.heading: User Account Registration

Whatever you give us needs to be accurate and current, and you'll need to keep it that way, especially your email and payment details, so we can actually process things and reach you if we need to. We handle registration data per our Privacy Policy. Keep your password to yourself.
Your Account ties to your personal email — no letting other people use it. You're on the hook for keeping your login secure and for anything that happens under your Account.

We can turn down a registration for good reason — a Terms violation, fraud concerns, doubts about who you are, suspected spam, uncertainty about your age, or trying to sign up from somewhere our Services aren't offered.

sections.heading: User Account Policy
paragraphs: Everything that happens under your Account is your responsibility. Don't use someone else's account, username, or password, and don't hand yours to anyone else.
Tell us right away if your Account's been accessed without permission.
If we have reason to think you've broken these Terms, or that something you told us was false, inaccurate, or incomplete, we can close your Account and cut off access to some or all Services.
We're not liable for any loss or damage from unauthorized access to or use of your Account.

sections.heading: Inactive User Account Policy

sections.heading: In-Game Purchases

To buy: pick your item in the Personal Cabinet, choose which Server it should go to, pay with an accepted method.
Once payment's confirmed, we'll get the Digital Item to your account on that Server without unnecessary delay.
If a payment fails or gets rejected by our payment provider, we're not obliged to complete the purchase.

Purchases have to come from your own account. We can refuse an order, or cap or cancel quantities per person, household, or order — including across orders using the same account, card, or billing details. Change or cancel an order, and we'll try to let you know using whatever contact details we have on file. We may also limit or refuse orders that look, in our judgement, like they're coming from resellers or distributors.
Keep your account and payment details accurate and current, so we can process purchases and reach you if needed.

sections.heading: Delivery Timeframes
paragraphs: Most purchases are delivered within seconds of payment confirmation. In rare cases — such as server maintenance or high load — delivery may take up to 24 hours.
If you have not received your items within 24 hours, please contact our support team with your order details.

sections.heading: Prices
paragraphs: Prices usually cover delivery, handling, and tax; if they don't, we'll say so before you order. Where you are might mean foreign exchange fees or different pricing.
We can adjust, pause, or drop any Service at our discretion, and we're not responsible for any losses that causes.
Where the law allows it, we can change prices whenever we like — you'll get reasonable notice, posted on the Website and/or sent by email or another obvious method.
Don't want to pay a new price? Cancel the relevant subscription before it kicks in — at least 24 hours before your current billing period ends, or you'll be charged.

sections.heading: Payments
paragraphs: Payments go on your account via debit card, credit card, or another accepted method.
Everything's paid upfront. You can only buy a Digital Item or Service if you've got the funds or credit to cover it.
Payment not approved, or bounced for insufficient funds? Your order doesn't go through.
Third-party providers handle all our payment processing. The Website just gets notified once payment's done — it doesn't store your card details.
Where it applies, we follow EU payment services law, including Directive (EU) 2015/2366 (PSD2).

sections.heading: Limitation of Liability
paragraphs: To whatever extent the law allows, the Company — along with our affiliates, agents, directors, employees, suppliers, and licensors — isn't liable for damages tied to your use, or inability to use, the Website, Content, Services, or Digital Items. That covers errors, interruptions, delays, lost data, unauthorized access, or relying on something you found through the Website.

We're never liable for indirect, special, incidental, consequential, punitive, or exemplary damages — lost goodwill, lost profits, corrupted or lost data, none of it. If you're unhappy with the Website, your only real option is to stop using it.
Our total liability to you, however it arises, won't exceed what you've actually paid us under these Terms.
This limit applies no matter the legal theory — contract, tort, negligence, strict liability, whatever — even if we've been told such damages were possible.

sections.heading: Disclaimer of Warranties
paragraphs: The Website, Content, and Services come "as is" and "as available," with no warranties of any kind — express or implied, including merchantability or fitness for a particular purpose — to the fullest extent the law allows.

We don't promise the Website or Services will match your specific needs, run without interruption, stay secure, be error-free, or that results will be accurate or reliable. Using the Website and our Servers is at your own risk.

sections.heading: Use of Game Servers and Compliance with Minecraft Usage Guidelines
paragraphs: Our Servers run subject to the Game's EULA and the Minecraft Usage Guidelines Mojang publishes (together, the "Minecraft Rules"). Mojang grants us these permissions at its own discretion, and can change or pull them at any time, without notice. If that happens, we might have to change, pause, or drop affected Services without owing you anything beyond what Section 15 already covers.

Don't use the Servers in ways that break the Minecraft Rules or the law, infringe on others' rights, overload or damage the Servers or connected networks, or try to get unauthorized access to the Servers or related systems. We can suspend or end your Server access anytime, with or without notice, for any reason.

Mojang can decide, entirely on its own, whether how we or our users monetize or use the Servers fits its guidelines — and it can pull these permissions whenever it wants. We reserve the right to change, restrict, or drop any Digital Item, privilege, or feature to stay compliant with the Minecraft Rules. To stay compliant, here's what applies to how you use the Servers and any Digital Items:
bullets: Server access only goes to users with a genuine, licensed copy of the Game.

Everything — Servers, Digital Items, any advertising on the Website or Servers — is all-ages appropriate. No gambling, pornography, violence, terrorism, explicit content, or other unsafe or mature material, anywhere in connection with our Services.

A "donation" means a payment with nothing exclusive coming back to the donor. If a payment gets someone a privilege, cosmetic, or benefit that other users don't get, that's a Digital Item purchase — and everything in these Terms and our [Billing, Refunds & Chargeback Policy](/billing-refunds) applies, whatever it's labelled as at checkout.

We don't sell, and you can't resell or help sell, any privilege, Digital Item, or entitlement that gives someone a competitive edge over other users, or that otherwise wrecks other users' experience of the Servers.
Cosmetic Digital Items on the Website won't visually copy a Minecraft Player Cape.

Crystals and any other virtual currency on the Website or Servers carry no real-world value — no cashing out, no redeeming for real money, no using them anywhere but our Servers, and nothing that looks like or claims to be Minecoins or any other Mojang or Microsoft currency.
You get an online purchase history for anything paid with real money, right there in your Personal Cabinet, and we publish pricing and Digital Item details on the Website before you buy.
We don't hide, change, or interfere with the Game's own dialogs, prompts, or messages — EULA notices, warnings, error messages, all of it stays as-is.
No malware, no spyware, no facilitating illegal activity through our Servers.
Influencers or creators we bring on to promote our Servers have to disclose their relationship with us, in line with applicable advertising rules — including FTC guidance, where it's relevant.

cookies.title: Cookie Policy
intro: This explains how Dexervil LTD uses cookies and similar tech on minecraftsgame.com. Read it alongside our Privacy Policy, which covers personal data more broadly.

sections.heading: What Cookies Actually Are
paragraphs: Cookies are small text files your browser stores when you visit a site. They let the site remember you — your device, your preferences, things you've done before. We also use a couple of related technologies, like local storage and pixels, and this Policy covers those too.

sections.heading: The Cookies We Use
paragraphs: The cookies on our site fall into a few categories:
bullets: Strictly Necessary — keep the Website working: staying logged in, secure checkout. Can't be turned off on our end.
Functional — remember things like your chosen Server or language.
Analytics — tell us how people actually use the Website (Google Analytics, for instance), so we can improve it.
Marketing — used only with your consent, to show more relevant ads and measure how well campaigns work.

sections.heading: Cookies Set by Others
paragraphs: Some of the cookies on our site aren't ours — they come from third parties providing things like analytics or payment processing. They follow their own cookie policies, which we don't control.

sections.heading: How Long They Stick Around
paragraphs: Cookies are either session-based or persistent:
bullets: Session cookies — gone the moment you close your browser.
Persistent cookies — stay until they expire or you delete them, so the site remembers you next time.

sections.heading: Your Cookie Choices
paragraphs: First visit, you'll see a banner asking you to consent to anything non-essential. You can change your mind later, whenever you like.

Your browser settings also let you manage or delete cookies directly — most browsers let you block them, wipe existing ones, or get a warning before one is set. Just know that blocking the strictly necessary ones may break things, like logging in or checking out.

sections.heading: If This Policy Changes
paragraphs: We may update this from time to time — new cookies, legal changes, whatever the reason. Worth a check back occasionally.

sections.heading: Questions?
paragraphs: Email privacy@minecraftsgame.com.

billing.title: Billing, Refunds & Chargeback Policy
intro: It is not an official Minecraft product. It is not approved by or associated with Mojang or Microsoft. Adventures in Minecraft is not supported by Mojang or Microsoft. It is not an official Minecraft platform. We provide our Services and sell our Digital Items in line with the Minecraft Usage Guidelines.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: Here's how billing works on https://minecraftsgame.com/ — how your balance and any recurring purchases are handled, and what to do if a charge looks wrong before you go to your bank about it. Buying a Digital Item, topping up your balance, or making any other purchase on the Website means you're agreeing to what follows. Read it alongside our Terms and Conditions, especially Sections 13, 14, and 17.

Purchases run through EUR (€) unless checkout says otherwise. We take Visa and Mastercard, processed securely by our payment provider, FINTECH GLOBAL SOFTWARE LTD, under PCI-DSS. Everything's tokenized; Dexervil LTD never sees or stores your full card number.

sections.heading: Billing and Your Balance, Explained
paragraphs: You can buy a Digital Item directly for a chosen Server, or top up a balance first and spend it as you go — including on recurring or subscription purchases (Section 4).

Top up your balance and the charge hits your payment method straight away, landing in your account balance the moment payment clears, in EUR or whatever currency you paid in. You'll see the balance in your Personal Cabinet, and it drops by the price of each Digital Item as you buy it.

Think of the balance as store credit, not money in a bank. It doesn't earn interest, can't be cashed out or swapped for cash, and can't move to another account or platform, except where the law says otherwise. It only buys Digital Items on this Website in line with the Minecraft Usage Guidelines covered in Section 17 of our Terms and Conditions.

sections.heading: What Happens to Your Balance If Your Account Closes
paragraphs: Close your account — whether that's you or us, under our Terms and Conditions — and any leftover balance goes one of two ways:
bullets: closed because you breached the Terms? The remaining balance may be forfeited, subject to the law;
closed for any other reason? You can ask for a refund of whatever's left, to your original payment method, once we've verified your identity and payment as described in Section 5;
either way, ask within 90 days of closure — after that, we may treat it as forfeited unless the law says we can't.

sections.heading: Purchases, Cancelling, and Refunds
paragraphs: 4.1 Individual purchases. Once a Digital Item lands in your Server account, that purchase is done — generally non-refundable, unless the law requires otherwise or we decide, at our discretion, that a refund makes sense (say, it never arrived, there was a delivery fault on our end, or you were charged the wrong amount). The full rundown of when refunds do and don't apply is in our Terms and Conditions.

4.2 Recurring and subscription purchases. Bought a privilege or rank on a recurring basis? Each charge counts as its own purchase and follows the same rules as 4.1. Cancel anytime, free, through your Personal Cabinet or by contacting us — details in Section 13 of the Terms and Conditions. Cancel at least 24 hours before the next billing date if you don't want to be charged again. Anything already delivered before you cancel stays yours.

4.3 Unused balance. Money sitting in your balance doesn't expire, though we may treat it as dormant after 90 days of inactivity — we'll reach out before touching anything, as the law requires. Outside of account closure (Section 3) or a legal requirement, unused balance isn't refundable.

4.4 Technical issues. Charged but the Digital Item never showed up because of a technical fault on our side? We'll credit it back to your balance or, if you'd rather and it's practical, refund your original payment method.

sections.heading: Getting Billing Support
paragraphs: Got a question about a charge? Talk to us before doing anything else, including a chargeback. Most issues — a Digital Item that didn't arrive, a charge you don't recognise, a recurring-purchase query — sort themselves out fast once we're actually looking at it together.
Email privacy@minecraftsgame.com with the following — the more you send upfront, the faster we can look into it:
bullets: the email address on your account;
roughly when the purchase happened;
the amount and currency charged;
which Digital Item and Server, if relevant;
a screenshot or copy of the payment confirmation or bank statement line;
a screenshot of your Personal Cabinet balance, if it's relevant.

sections.heading: How Fast We Respond
paragraphs: We aim to acknowledge billing and chargeback queries within 2 business days, and to have a resolution or decision within 10 business days of getting everything we asked for in Section 5.

sections.heading: Chargebacks
paragraphs: Try us first, through Section 5 — it's almost always quicker than going through your bank. That said, if a chargeback comes in for a charge that was properly authorised, where the Digital Item was actually delivered, or where we've already sorted things out under this Policy, we reserve the right to dispute it and to suspend or limit your account while it's being looked at.

sections.heading: Staying in Line with Minecraft Usage Guidelines
paragraphs: Mojang's Usage Guidelines shape how we run billing here. In practice that means: pricing and Digital Item details are published on the Website before you buy anything; you get an online purchase history for anything paid with real money, through your Personal Cabinet; and your balance, along with any crystals or other in-game currency, has no real-world value and can't be cashed out, redeemed, or moved off the Website or our Servers. None of this overrides Section 17 of our Terms and Conditions.
